macros.name: arrlabel
macros.doc: This command is a version of LaTeX’s ordinary \label{FOO} command meant to be used in deqarr and ddeqar environments. In these environments, a \label{FOO} command gives a reference to the specific equation, e.g. 3b, whereas \arrlabel{FOO} in the same position gives a reference containing only the main equation number, 3 in this example.

macros.name: deleqno
macros.doc: Gives a partial equation number when used within $$ ... $$.

macros.name: heqno
macros.doc: Used within deqarr and ddeqar environments to step the main equation number by one and to produce an ordinary equation number; thus, gives equation number ‘4’ when following equation ‘3c’.

macros.name: nydeleqno
macros.doc: Gives a new partial equation number when used within $$ ... $$.

macros.name: nydeqno
macros.doc: Used within deqarr and ddeqar environments to step the main equation number by one and reset the partial equation number to ‘a’; thus, \nydeqno gives equation number ‘4a’ when following after equation ‘3c’.

macros.name: rdeqno
macros.doc: Same as \rndeqno{FOO} but without resetting any equation number counter and giving consecutive partial equation numbers (‘4b’, ‘4c’, etc.).

macros.name: rem
macros.doc: The command \rem{text} typsets the text “text” (in the default LR-font) flush left on a seperate row in eqnarray, deqarr, ddeqar, and deqrarr environments, and preserves the environment’s alignment for rows to come.

macros.name: reqno
macros.doc: Is used when repeating an equation with its original number, “recycling” the eqaution number. \reqno takes the argument FOO, which has to be defined by a \label{FOO} in the original equation.

macros.name: rndeqno
macros.doc: Adds a partial equation number to an old equation number, specified by the FOO label.

macros.name: where
macros.doc: The command \where typsets the text “where” (in the default LR-font) flush left on a seperate row in eqnarray, deqarr, ddeqar, and deqrarr environments, and preserves the environment’s alignment for rows to come.

envs.name: ddeqar
envs.doc: Typesets an equation array just like \begin{eqnarray} ... \end{eqnarray} does, but gives the equation numbers such as ‘3a’ if following after an equation numbered ‘3’ (ordinary equation number) and numbers such as ‘3c’ if following after a partially numbered equation ‘3b’.

envs.name: deqarr
envs.doc: Typesets an equation array just like \begin{eqnarray} ... \end{eqnarray} does, but gives the first numbered equation a number like ‘3a’ instead of ‘3’ (always ‘a’), and the following ‘3b’, ‘3c’ etc. It steps the main equation counter.

envs.name: deqn
envs.doc: Typesets an equation just like \begin{equation} ... \end{equation} does, but gives it a number such as ‘3a’ instead of ‘3’ (always ‘a’).

envs.name: deqrarr
envs.doc: This environment is meant to host recycled equations and has eqnarray structure.
